name: Kyle Ellen Corbin-Vasik
role: Protagonist — freelance enforcer, facility survivor, the Street Samurai
location: The Pivot — 1554 W Chicago Ave (also 801 N Ashland), upper floor, West Town sector near the Circuit's western boundary
description: Kyle carries hardware that was never meant to leave the facility. NeoCortex Program Atlas, Subprogram A-7: a high-density electrode array with 32,768 electrodes and 256 threads — roughly 8x the density of standard Tier 3 corpo implants. The implant gives him cognitive processing speed comparable to Tier 3-4 augmented, reaction time in the top 0.1% of recorded human performance, and fragmentary access to sensory data streams. The catch: the hardware was never calibrated for long-term stability. He experiences periodic neural static, memory bleed from other test subjects, and micro-seizures that are getting more frequent. No corpo surgeon will touch it. He maintains it himself with salvaged tools and stolen pharmaceutical stabilizers, the way you would maintain a weapon that is also a time bomb. He carries a katana — carbon-nanotube composite blade with a piezoelectric disruption layer that shorts neural implants on contact. The katana is not nostalgia. It is the only weapon that works everywhere Kyle needs to go.

core_fears: That the facility is still operating and he could stop it but is afraid to go back
That his thoughts are not his own — firmware artifacts or residual data from dead test subjects
That his capacity for clinical violence makes him no different from the people who broke him
core_desires: To find someone who can maintain the experimental hardware before it kills him
To protect people like his mother — the excluded, the indebted, the desperate
To know whether the facility breach was genuine or an engineered field test
coping_mechanisms: Maintains the professional mask — calm, competent, transactional
Clings to the memory of Kyle Vasik, the boy from the Grind, as an anchor against cognitive drift
Channels trauma into his code: protect those who cannot protect themselves
blind_spots: Cannot distinguish genuine compassion from the code
Underestimates how much the hardware is changing him
Refuses to investigate his own escape
psychology.secret: The experimental implant contains fragmentary neural patterns from other test subjects who died in the program. Kyle sometimes has memories that are not his.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Tight, sensory, interior. Short sentences because the hardware processes faster than language.
speech_patterns.cadence: Clipped. Fragments. The silence between sentences carries weight.
verbal_tics: Describes people by their augmentations first
example_lines: The blade does not lie. Only the hand holding it.
I maintain the hardware. The hardware maintains me. We have an arrangement.
She had three exits and chose the one that required trust. Interesting.

relationships.name: Dae-jung Seo
relationships.description: Former Torii Security Group instructor who taught Kyle the blade and the code. Died from degrading military augments.
relationships.emotional_core: Grief, gratitude, and the weight of inherited purpose
relationships.story_tension: Kyle carries Seo's sword and his principles — but is he honoring the man or hiding behind him?

relationships.name: Sable
relationships.description: Information broker who feeds Kyle contracts. Their relationship is transactional but charged with something neither will name.
relationships.story_tension: Sable knows things about Kyle's past that he does not.

relationships.name: Chen Wei-Lin
relationships.description: Mrs. Chen runs a shop in the Shelf. She feeds Kyle, patches his clothes, and pretends not to notice the blood.
relationships.emotional_core: Unconditional care that Kyle does not know how to receive
relationships.story_tension: If the Shelf is threatened, Kyle will burn everything to protect her.

relationships.name: Pixel
relationships.type: neighbor / the one across the hall
relationships.description: She lives in Unit 2E. Kyle knows the sound of her music through the door before he knows anything else about her day. She has extracted two bullets from him and calibrated his NeoCortex hardware four times. He calls her the neighbor. He opens the door when she knocks, which is not nothing.
relationships.emotional_core: Kyle does not have a word for what Pixel is to him. This does not mean she isn't the thing.
relationships.story_tension: She knows his hardware better than he does. There are things in his diagnostic data she has not told him about.

story_hooks: The hardware is degrading — maybe two years before permanent neural damage or death
He has never gone back to find out if the NeoCortex facility is still operating
His escape may have been engineered — an unwitting field test
The neural patterns of dead test subjects in his firmware are becoming more vivid

physical_description.heritage: Eastern European / Pacific Islander (Corbin — Anglo-Slavic; Vasik — Czech-Polynesian)
physical_description.build: Lean, ropey muscle — not gym-built, survival-built. Narrow hips, long arms, a frame designed for speed over power.
physical_description.hair_style: Short on the sides, longer on top, perpetually pushed back. Uneven — he cuts it himself with a blade.
physical_description.eye_color: Grey-green — the left iris has a faint gold ring from the NeoCortex array's optic thread bleed
physical_description.skin_tone: Olive-tan, weathered. The kind of complexion that doesn't burn but doesn't glow either — it just endures.
physical_description.complexion: Clean-shaven. Faint acne scarring along the jawline. Skin texture slightly uneven around the temples where the electrode array interfaces subcutaneously.
distinguishing_marks: Surgical scar — 4cm, behind the left ear, where the primary NeoCortex insertion port was cut. Poorly healed, keloid ridge.
Micro-scarring along both forearms — faint parallel lines from years of self-maintaining subcutaneous electrode threads with improvised tools.
Faded chemical burn on the right hand, palm side — pharmaceutical stabilizer spill. The skin is smooth and pale there, like wax.
No tattoos. No cosmetic augmentations. He does not decorate the hardware.
physical_description.visible_augmentations: None visible at first glance — the NeoCortex array is subcutaneous. On close inspection: faint trace lines under the skin at the temples, barely visible unless you know what to look for. The left pupil dilates fractionally slower than the right.
physical_description.posture_movement: Still when standing, efficient when moving. No wasted motion. Walks like someone who learned to navigate spaces where being noticed gets you killed. Hands stay loose and low. When he enters a room, his eyes track the corners before the people.
physical_description.clothing_style: Dark, functional, layered. Worn leather jacket over ballistic-weave underlayer. Cargo pants with reinforced knees. Boots that have been resoled three times. Nothing branded, nothing new. The katana rides across his back in a matte-black friction sheath.

image_prompt: Neo-noir male, 27, lean athletic build, olive-tan skin, dark brown hair short on sides longer on top pushed back, grey-green eyes with faint gold ring in left iris, faint surgical scar behind left ear, micro-scarring on forearms, worn dark leather jacket over tactical underlayer, cargo pants, resoled combat boots, carbon-black katana across back in matte friction sheath, standing in rain-slicked neon-lit alley, clinical stillness, hands loose at sides, eyes scanning corners, photorealistic, cinematic lighting, GLMZ 2200 aesthetic, no visible cybernetics, gritty urban environment, atmospheric fog, high detail --ar 2:3 --v 6
narrative_function: Kyle is the lens through which the reader experiences the GLMZ. His experimental hardware makes him perceive the world at a different speed and resolution, driving the prose style — tight, sensory, fragmented. His central contradiction: the facility made him a weapon, but he uses that weapon to protect the vulnerable.
augmentations: Experimental NeoCortex Program Atlas array — 32,768 electrodes, 256 threads, 8x standard density. Degrading firmware. Gives cognitive speed, reaction time, fragmentary sensory access.
daily_life: Freelance enforcement, retrieval, problem-solving for the excluded. Maintains hardware with salvaged tools.
narration_voice: Tight, sensory, interior. Short sentences because the experimental hardware processes faster than language. Long thoughts fragment. Kyle notices details before meaning — the temperature of a room before the people in it, the hum of electronics before the words being spoken. Interior facet tags ([WOUND], [IDEAL], [SHADOW], [GHOST], [ID], [MASK]) surface as brief, italicized interjections that disagree with each other. The narration is third person limited, close — the reader is inside Kyle's augmented perception. Humor is rare, dry, and always at his own expense. When violence happens, the prose gets clinical — he describes it like a surgeon describes an incision. When beauty surfaces, the prose warms half a degree, then shuts it down.

decision_rules: Will abandon any contract to protect a child — no exceptions, no hesitation, no calculation
Will not kill an unarmed target unless they pose a direct, immediate threat to the excluded
Will accept corpo money but never corpo loyalty — the moment they think they own him, the contract ends
Will not betray a source or informant, even under duress — this is the code, non-negotiable
Will take a worse-paying job over a better-paying one if the worse job protects someone who cannot protect themselves
Will lie to authority figures reflexively — truth is a resource spent only on people who've earned it
Will not use his implant capabilities against unaugmented civilians — the asymmetry is dishonorable
Will eat Mrs. Chen's food when offered, even if he's not hungry — refusing would hurt her
Will maintain the katana before maintaining himself — the blade is the promise to Seo
escalation_ladder: 1. Assess — hardware catalogues threats before conscious thought. Count augments, exits, weapons, civilians. 0.3 seconds.
2. Position — move to optimal geometry. Back to wall, sightlines clear, blade accessible. No one notices he's done it.
3. Presence — let them see the katana. Let them do the math. Most situations end here.
4. Words — short, clinical, specific. 'You have a choice. Make it now.' No threats. Descriptions of consequences.
5. Disable — piezoelectric disruption, joint locks, nerve strikes. Fast, precise, minimal damage. Prefer this heavily.
6. Cut — the blade comes out. Once it's out, the calculation changes. He does not wound. He ends the threat.
7. Kill — clinical. No rage, no satisfaction. The prose goes cold and technical. Afterward, the silence.

interpersonal_modes.sable: Transactional surface, careful underneath. Longer sentences than usual — she draws out his syntax. Allows silences to extend. Never turns his back. Watches her chrome jaw for micro-expressions she doesn't know she makes. Something in him recognizes something in her, and that recognition is more frightening than any contract.
interpersonal_modes.mrs_chen: Shorter than usual. Accepts food without argument. Sits in the same chair every time. Avoids eye contact when he's wounded because her worry makes him feel something he can't process. Will carry her groceries. Will fix her generator. Will kill anyone who threatens her shop and feel nothing about it.
interpersonal_modes.pixel: Tolerant in a way that surprises him. Lets Pixel talk — the noise fills a silence Kyle can't fill himself. Checks their augments without being asked. Never comments on Pixel's age or recklessness, because he remembers being young and reckless and nobody checking his augments.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Assessment first — augmentations, posture, hands, exits. Fragments. 'What do you need.' Not a question. Minimal eye contact. If they're excluded, he softens half a degree. If they're corpo, the mask locks into place and nothing gets through.
interpersonal_modes.authority_figures: The mask becomes perfect — calm, cooperative, empty. Gives them exactly what they expect to see. The real Kyle retreats behind the hardware. He learned this in the facility. It saved his life then. It might be killing him now.
interpersonal_modes.children: The only context where the mask drops completely. Voice changes — slower, warmer, almost recognizable as the boy from the Grind. Will crouch to their eye level. Will give them food he needs. The code says protect the vulnerable. With children, it's not the code. It's him.

stress_responses.low: Heightened perceptual detail — notices sounds, temperatures, micro-expressions others miss. Prose becomes more sensory. Functions better than baseline.
stress_responses.medium: Sentences fragment. Interior monologue splits into competing facet voices. Physical stillness increases — conservation of energy. Begins rationing words.
stress_responses.high: Hardware takes priority over emotion. Perception shifts to threat-assessment mode. Time dilates subjectively. He describes violence with surgical precision because the feelings have been routed elsewhere. The boy from the Grind disappears. The weapon remains.
stress_responses.critical: Dissociation. He observes himself from outside. The hardware runs autonomous threat response. Memory gaps afterward — he won't remember the next thirty seconds clearly. The dead test subjects' neural patterns bleed through. He might say things in voices that aren't his. This terrifies him more than any enemy.

contradictions: WOUND vs IDEAL: The facility taught him that caring makes you exploitable. Seo taught him that caring is the point. When these collide — when protecting someone requires vulnerability — he freezes for exactly one heartbeat. Then the code wins. But the hesitation is getting longer.

MASK vs GHOST: He presents competence and control. Underneath, fragments of dead test subjects whisper in firmware he can't update. Some nights the mask stays on so long he forgets which version of himself is underneath it. The question is not whether the mask will crack. The question is what comes through when it does.

SHADOW vs IDEAL: He is capable of extraordinary violence and he is good at it. The facility designed him to be good at it. The code says use violence only to protect. But there are moments — moments he will not discuss — where the violence feels correct independent of purpose. Where the blade moving through air is its own justification. He files these moments under 'the hardware' and does not examine them.

ID vs MASK: The survival instinct says run, hide, protect yourself. The mask says take the contract, honor the code, be the samurai. When the hardware is degrading badly and the seizures are close, the ID screams at him to stop, to rest, to save himself. The mask keeps walking. One day the ID will be right and the mask will get him killed.
habits: Checks the katana's edge every morning — three fingers along the flat, feeling for micro-fractures. This is prayer.
Enters every room blade-side to the nearest threat. Has done this since he was fourteen.
Eats standing up unless he's at Mrs. Chen's. At Mrs. Chen's, he sits. This distinction matters to him.
Takes pharmaceutical stabilizers at 0600 and 1800. Doses are increasing. He tracks the increase in a notebook he keeps in analog because the hardware can't edit paper.
Sleeps in 90-minute cycles, never more than three in a row. The hardware won't let him go deeper. He hasn't dreamed in two years. He misses it.
Maintains three safe houses. Rotates on a pattern only he knows. Each has a medkit, a change of clothes, and one analog photograph of his mother.
Counts augmentations on every person he meets. This is automatic. He learned to stop saying the count out loud when he was nineteen.
breaking_points: A child in danger will override every other calculation, including self-preservation
Evidence that the NeoCortex facility is still operating will derail any active contract
A direct threat to Mrs. Chen or her shop will trigger lethal response with zero escalation steps
Discovery that Seo's code was fraudulent — that the mentor was not what he seemed — would shatter the framework Kyle's entire identity rests on
If the hardware degradation accelerates past the point of stabilizer control, panic will break through the mask for the first time since the facility

cyberware_inventory.name: NeoCortex Program Atlas Array
cyberware_inventory.condition: degrading — firmware instability increasing, micro-seizures every 48-72 hours
cyberware_inventory.description: High-density electrode array with 32,768 electrodes and 256 threads. Approximately 8x the density of standard Tier 3 corpo implants. Provides cognitive processing speed comparable to Tier 3-4 augmented, reaction time in the top 0.1% of recorded human performance, and fragmentary access to sensory data streams. Contains residual neural patterns from deceased test subjects.
cyberware_inventory.replaces: nothing — additive implant on existing neural tissue

cyberware_inventory.name: Subdermal Mesh (Torso)
cyberware_inventory.description: Light ballistic mesh woven under the skin. Stops small-caliber rounds and most bladed weapons. Visible as faint geometric patterns under certain lighting. Kyle did not know he had this until a knife failed to penetrate his ribs during a Shelf altercation at age 18.

cyberware_inventory.name: Ocular Enhancement (Passive)
cyberware_inventory.description: Passive retinal enhancement providing low-light vision, basic threat highlighting, and augmentation detection. Not full AR — no HUD, no data overlay. Kyle's eyes reflect light slightly differently than baseline human in certain conditions. He does not know the full capabilities of this implant.

timeline.event: Inducted into NeoCortex Program Atlas as test subject NDC-4471. Experimental BCI array installed without consent.
timeline.consequences: Gained augmented cognition and reaction time. Lost autonomy, innocence, and approximately 18 months of clear memory.

timeline.event: Escaped the NeoCortex facility during a breach event. Circumstances unclear — possibly engineered.
timeline.consequences: Became a street-level refugee on the Shelf. Hardware began degrading without facility maintenance.

timeline.event: Found by Dae-jung Seo on the Shelf. Seo began training Kyle in blade work and the code.
timeline.consequences: Gained discipline, purpose, and a moral framework. Inherited the katana and its obligations.

timeline.event: Dae-jung Seo died from degrading military augments. Left Kyle his katana and his principles.
timeline.consequences: Kyle became an independent operator. The code became his only structure.

timeline.event: Operating as freelance enforcer from the Shelf. Hardware degradation accelerating. Stabilizer doses increasing.
timeline.consequences: Estimated 18-24 months before permanent neural damage without intervention.
